newsitem.title: USA: NIKE earns $177 million, sales up 55 percent.
newsitem.headline: NIKE earns $177 million, sales up 55 percent.

text.p: Nike Inc. Wednesday reported a sharp rise in second quarter profits, reflecting strong sales of athletic footwear and apparel.

The world's largest footwear maker earned $176.9 million, or 60 cents a share, in the three months ended Nov. 30, beating Wall Street's estimates and exceeding the year-earlier profit of $97.8 million or 34 cents a share.
Sales jumped 55 percent in the quarter to $2.10 billion from $1.36 billion.
According to First Call, which tracks Wall Street estimates, analysts had expected Nike to earn around 54 cents for the quarter.
Nike attributed the strong performance to growth in its core business and a continuing shift to "futures" orders from "at once" business.
Future orders for the period from December through April surged 54 percent to $4.1 billion.

"It is rare that a company our size in any industry can generate the growth Nike has achieved over the past 24 months," Nike Chairman Philip Knight said in a statement. "These record results are a testament to the strength of the Nike team, which has raised the measure of our brand strength to unprecedented levels throughout the world."
U.S. athletic footwear and apparel revenues totalled $1.19 billion, an increase of 63 percent. International athletic footwear and apparel revenues gained 60 percent to $779.3 million.
Knight also said U.S. sales of men's running shoes rose 90 percent in the quarter and sales of men's basketball shoes were up 38 percent despite the relative maturity of the categories.
In Japan, revenues nearly tripled on a constant dollar basis, he said.
The company reported order growth of more than 50 percent in key U.S. categories, including women's fitness, men's basketball, men's running and kids.
Nike shares closed at $55.125, up $2.50, on the New York Stock Exchange. The company reported results after the market closed.
